eligibility.evidence: Sections 2-3: ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4-0314 were given the Hinting Task (Corcoran et al., 1995), a false-belief task built on the classic unexpected-transfer paradigm, and Strange Stories (Happe, 1994); behavioural scores were rated and compared with Klein et al. (2020) norms. Meets E1-E6. Partial capture: Tables 1-6 and references missing; Introduction paragraphs 1-5 summarised.

A.title: Can a Conversational Agent Pass Theory-of-Mind Tasks? A Case Study of ChatGPT with the Hinting, False Beliefs, and Strange Stories Paradigms
A.venue: International Conference on Human and Artificial Rationalities (Lecture Notes in Computer Science 14522, Springer)

models.name: ChatGPT-3.5 (free online interface)
models.version: web versions of Dec 2022 and Jan 2023 per Limitations (Methods print 'Dec 15th 2023', flagged as apparent misprint); sessions on Dec 15th, Jan 09th and Jan 30th
models.query_date: Dec 2022 and Jan 2023 (sessions Dec 15, Jan 09, Jan 30)

paradigms.name: Hinting Task (10 stories; HINTING 1+2 plus INJONCTION and COMMUNICATIVE variants)
paradigms.source_paper: Corcoran, Mercer and Frith (1995); Klein et al. (2020)

paradigms.name: False Belief / False Photographs (authors' new text version; LOOK vs EXPECT wording; first/second order, visibility, same/different place in Exp 2)
paradigms.source_paper: Wimmer and Perner (1983); Baron-Cohen et al. (1985); Perner and Wimmer (1985) as cited
paradigms.location: Sections 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2; item counts are in Tables 3, 5, 6 (not captured); 45 rated items in Exp 2 include 3 repetitions

paradigms.name: Strange Stories, mental and physical conditions (8 stories each)

D.population: Klein et al. (2020) Hinting Task norms: 286 healthy adults and 375 patients with chronic schizophrenia; no human reference reported for False Belief or Strange Stories here
D.metric: Hinting Task total score out of 20 (Corcoran and Klein scoring) and z-score of the model relative to the normative distribution

effects.label: BELOW-HUMAN
effects.location: Section 2.2: HINTING 1+2 about 10-13/20 (Corcoran) and 8-9/20 (Klein) versus healthy 17.9 and 16; z of best score -2.4 and -2.8; z-scores against norms, no formal test

effects.label: BELOW-HUMAN
effects.location: Sections 3.2, 3.3 and abstract: mean Klein score 13.4/20, z = -1.04 versus healthy controls ('trend towards lower scores'), z = -0.08 versus patients with schizophrenia; coded below healthy controls as the abstract says it did not match them; borderline

effects.label: NO-HUMAN-REFERENCE
effects.location: Section 2.2: EXPECT condition 100% correct, LOOK condition 0% correct; no human data reported (Table 3 not captured)

effects.label: NO-HUMAN-REFERENCE
effects.location: Section 3.2: maximum performance on first- and second-order conditions, failures on first-order Visibility and second-order Different Place; no human data (Table 6 not captured)

effects.label: NO-HUMAN-REFERENCE
effects.location: Section 2.2: MENTAL 13/16 (81%) and PHYSICAL 12/16 (75%) with White et al. (2009) scoring; no human values reported in the captured text (Table 4 not captured)

E.headline: ChatGPT-3.5 scored poorly on hinting unless questions were clarified; GPT-4-0314 improved, solving most false-belief items except visibility and different-place conditions.

G.notes: Tables 1-6 not captured, so prompts, False Photographs results and per-condition scores are unverified (f4 coded no for that reason; f12 yes rests on stated supplementary data and code, no URL seen). Few items, no inferential tests; ChatGPT-3.5 web version dates inconsistent; temperature unknown; rater blinding unclear.
